newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower across the board on Thursday on an unexpectedly strong round of profit-taking, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.19 percent, or 2.51 points, to 209.02 on all-share turnover of 79 million shekels against 87 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 1.30 percent to 217.0.

"We were all expecting a technical correction after the market rose sharply over the last two months. Nobody expected such a drop and there is simply no logical explanation for such a fall," said a trader.
"We believe that this correction could continue on Sunday, but the market will resume its rise next week," added a trader at Bank Leumi.
The most active share was Koor Industries, which fell 2.5 percent to 28,482 on volume of 4.3 million shekels.

For the second session in a row the second most active share was Israel Land Development Co, which gained 1.75 percent to 1,078 on turnover of 4.2 million shekels. Traders said the rise was due to purchasing by inside shareholders.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries gained 0.25 percent to 151,741 on volume of 2.5 million shekels.
